title: He hoped there would be stew for dinner, turnips and carrots and bruised potatoes and fat mutton pieces to be ladled out in thick peppered flour-fattened sauce. Stuff it into you, his belly counselled him
html_source: This part of Chapter 3 comes just after Stephen Dedalus has a casual encounter with a prostitute for the first time. It seems almost too coincidental that he is now exhibiting signs of gluttony in the way he is longing for large amounts of food. Both of these situations feature one of the seven deadly sins recognized by the Christian church, and they depict Stephen’s descent from the graces of God into the world of sin. Both of these sins can be characterized by the temptation they cause in Stephen as he is reluctant to make a move on the prostitute at first, but eventually succumbs. Similarly, it can be argued that Stephen’s hunger causes him to fetishize food in a sinful manner.
